# Identify-before-absence — probe the FULL artifact-class space before claiming "does not exist"

"X does not exist" is a per-class verdict, available only after probing every root of that
class (or the registry that indexes them) — never from one or two directories, a failed
call, or an unloaded schema.

## WHY — measured
- 2026-09-30: `harness-self-improve-sweep` was declared nonexistent after probing only
  skills/commands; it was a workflow — live in BOTH roots (`C:\Users\Prekzursil\.claude\workflows\harness-self-improve-sweep-important.js`,
  Glob-verified this run) and indexed twice in `~/.agents/knowledge/workflows-registry.md:18,32`.
- Tool-shaped twin (2026-09-22, wf_c8e4c79c-1c8): a failed call is a transport event —
  owned by `native-capability-map.md`, not restated here.
- Indexes manufacture absence too: 179 skills invisible to routing for 3 months
  (`derived-index-freshness.md`) — a stale discovery layer hides real artifacts.
- SOTA: deferred tool schemas mean "not loaded" ≠ "does not exist"
  (anthropic.com/engineering/advanced-tool-use); MCP `Unknown tool` is server-scoped, never
  global (modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools); skill listings
  silently truncate under context budget (code.claude.com/docs/en/skills).

## Mechanics — the class space (probe ALL roots, or cite the registry)
- skills / commands / agents: `~/.agents/skills` (SSOT) + `~/.claude/{skills,commands,agents}`
  (materialized sync targets)
- workflows: `~/.claude/workflows` (incl. `_bak_*/`, `scripts/`, `snippets/`) +
  `~/.agents/workflows` + repo `agent-self/config/workflows` + session-embedded —
  SSOT index: `~/.agents/knowledge/workflows-registry.md` (regen
  `scripts/build-workflow-registry.py`; 542 entries by class counts, 2026-09-30)
- MCP: ToolSearch catalog + `~/.agents/agents.json`; name collisions across servers can
  fake BOTH presence and absence — disambiguate before concluding either
- plugins / hooks: `claude plugin list`; `~/.claude/hooks/` + `hooks/_dispatch/manifest.json`

## Discipline
1. Name the artifact class, then probe every root above (Glob/Grep) or read the registry —
   and check its `Generated:` stamp first: a stale index is not an absence oracle.
2. Absence needs a SECOND mechanically independent probe (`single-signal-verification.md`):
   registry grep + filesystem Glob, or ToolSearch + a different transport.
3. State the scope in the claim: "not in <roots probed>", never bare "nonexistent".
4. Failed call / unloaded schema / server-scoped "Unknown tool" routes to
   `native-capability-map.md` (change transport, not the capability claim).
5. A class with no index is itself the finding: build the registry before trusting absence.

Siblings: `native-capability-map.md` (tool failure ≠ absence) · `single-signal-verification.md`
(absence corroboration) · `derived-index-freshness.md` (index rot) · `research-coverage.md`
(the complement read).

# Method-proposal-before-execution (propose the shape before spending tokens)

**Rule:** for any non-trivial task, PROPOSE the method/architecture — topology (loop | pipeline/DAG | parallel barrier | loop-until-dry | judge-panel | map-reduce | tree search), sequencing, and verification shape — BEFORE executing or writing, so the owner can steer the shape while steering is still cheap. Owner directive, 2026-09-30.

## WHY — measured evidence
- MAST, "Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?" (arXiv 2503.13657; 150 traces, kappa 0.88):
  2 of the 3 failure classes are **system design issues** and **task verification** — the exact
  fields this proposal forces into the open before any tokens are spent on the wrong shape.
  [almost certain 0.90-0.95 — abstract fetched + corroborated]
- ReWOO (arXiv 2305.18323): plan-once-upfront = **5x token efficiency, +4% accuracy** (HotpotQA)
  vs observe-per-step. [almost certain 0.90-0.95]
- LLMCompiler (arXiv 2312.04511): plan-as-DAG + replanning = **up to 3.7x latency, 6.7x cost
  savings** vs sequential ReAct — SOTA is plan + replan path, not one static plan. [almost certain]
- Anthropic multi-agent research system: multi-agent ≈ **15x chat tokens**; fits breadth-first
  parallelizable work, NOT dependency-dense coding — topology choice IS the cost decision.
  [almost certain — primary fetched]
- Claude Code plan mode and LangGraph plan-and-execute both institutionalize
  proposal → approval → execute → replan with an explicit gate. [almost certain — official docs]

## Mechanics — the 6-field proposal (one block, before first execution)
[Format is a derived synthesis of the sources above — estate convention, not a cited spec — UNVERIFIED as a single-source format]
1. **GOAL** — one line, restated (AGENTS-RUNTIME §1).
2. **TOPOLOGY** — from the vocabulary above + a one-line task-shape rationale:
   parallelizable? context-exceeding? dependency-dense? verifiable?
3. **STEPS** — ordered/DAG list, named tool + model per step, ReWOO-style #E1/#E2 references
   so downstream steps compose without re-feeding observations.
4. **VERIFY** — accept criteria + who/what checks them (the MAST "task verification" class).
5. **REPLAN** — trigger (step fails / evidence contradicts plan) + fallback topology.
6. **BUDGET** — step/token ceiling, justified against the 15x multi-agent datum.

## Discipline
- **Non-trivial tasks only.** Trivial/routine ops proceed directly (§1 EVPI gate; owner-ops
  doctrines 7-8 — permission theater is banned). The proposal is a steering surface, not a brake.
- **Wide or irreversible scope ⇒ blocking approval gate** (plan-mode semantics); otherwise
  propose-and-proceed in the same turn.
- Proposal happens BEFORE execution, never mid-task (§1); once approved, execute to completion
  and replan only on the declared trigger.
- **Single-agent loop is the DEFAULT topology**; tree/DAG/panel must earn their ~15x cost in the
  task-shape rationale line. Judge-panel is the exception that scales with agent count
  (arXiv 2402.05120) — use it when verification-by-diversity is the bottleneck.
- The proposal FOLDS IN §1's goal restate and §1b's assumption ledger for the task it covers —
  it replaces those artifacts, it does not stack on top of them.
- Fan-out chosen ⇒ `fan-out-contract.md` governs the spawn prompts; cross-vendor dispatch ⇒
  `cross-vendor-dispatch.md`; research task ⇒ `research-coverage.md` digest first.

## Siblings
`development-workflow.md` (step-1 Plan First names the METHOD, not just steps) ·
`fan-out-contract.md` · `agents.md` · `cross-vendor-dispatch.md` ·
`single-signal-verification.md` (VERIFY floor) · `owner-ops-authorization.md` (the scope cut).

langchain.com/blog/planning-agents; code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.

# task-list-above-session-context

**Rule:** Session context is NOT the boundary of work state — consult the cross-session registers (TASKBOX, OPEN-LOOPS, DIRECTIVES, the workflows registry) BEFORE starting work and AGAIN before declaring anything done; when in-session recollection and a register disagree on position, the register wins.

## WHY — measured evidence

- Owner directive 2026-09-30 (G-3/Q9 scope change): deferred items live above any single session; a session that never consults the registers silently drops in-flight work.
- The registers exist because lifetimes differ (AGENTS-RUNTIME §1d: TASKBOX = hours-days, OPEN-LOOPS = until someone does it, DIRECTIVES = never closes) — "conflating them is why things get lost."
- Precedence shape is already estate doctrine for the ledger: SessionStart replay is trusted "as ground truth, not any in-context summary" (AGENTS-RUNTIME §3). This rule extends that shape to the registers at both boundaries.
- SOTA corroboration (primary-source fetched this run, 2026-09-30):
  - Manus: file system = "the ultimate context: unlimited in size, persistent by nature"; the todo list is rewritten step-by-step as a deliberate attention mechanism — https://manus.im/blog/Context-Engineering-for-AI-Agents-Lessons-from-Building-Manus (almost certain 93%).
  - Anthropic: compaction must preserve "architectural decisions, unresolved bugs"; agents re-read their own notes after context resets — https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents (almost certain 93%).
  - Claude Code memory docs: project CLAUDE.md is re-read from disk after /compact; instructions are "context, not enforced configuration"; subagents do NOT inherit auto memory — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory (almost certain 93%).
  - Beads: `bd prime` is the deterministic session-start re-anchor; "Do not use markdown TODO lists for task tracking" — https://github.com/gastownhall/beads README (almost certain 92%).

## Mechanics

- **Start boundary** (before the first substantive action, and after every compaction/resume): PULL — TASKBOX (in-flight), OPEN-LOOPS (owner + review-by), DIRECTIVES (standing, judged BENEFICIAL/CONDITIONAL/COSTLY), workflows registry (in-flight Workflow/fan-out runs and their journals, e.g. `bd prime --work-type recovery`, agent-monitor state). Pull, never assume.
- **Done boundary** (before any "done/complete/shipped" claim): re-read the registers. Anything the work touched but did not finish is resolved in-turn or written to a register with owner + review-by — never dropped.
- **Precedence scope:** register > session recollection for POSITION and STEERING (what is left, deferred, owned). Rebuild the plan from the register and say so. This NEVER extends to evidence — a register row is bookkeeping, not verification (hooks.md: "progress bookkeeping is NOT verification").
- **Subagents:** registers are not inherited — every spawn receives task state as an explicit structured handoff (AGENTS-RUNTIME §5); raw parent context is never the handoff.
- **Rewrite, don't append:** update the row as state changes; decay/archive closed items or the register becomes the bloat it prevents (context-reduction.md anti-bloat bar).
- **Enforcement pairing:** this rule is context, not enforcement — the gap-check Stop hook reads the registers mechanically; keep that lane intact.

## Discipline

- NEVER treat "not in my session" as "not my problem" — that is the orphaned-deferral defect (lane A defers, lane B edits, nobody owns).
- NEVER declare done while a register shows an in-scope open item you created or touched — finish it or re-register it with owner + review-by.
- NEVER let in-context recollection override a register on position; when they disagree, rebuild from the register.
- NEVER cite register state as completion EVIDENCE — position only; claims still need independent verification (single-signal-verification.md).
- ALWAYS hand register-derived position to every spawned subagent explicitly.
- ALWAYS end a boundary check with either "registers clean for this scope" or a register write — silence is not a check.

## Siblings

- `hooks.md` — in-session Task-tool tracking; the "NOT verification" boundary this rule respects.
- `context-reduction.md` — compaction preserves decisions/diffs/OPEN-LOOPS; the anti-bloat bar.
- `single-signal-verification.md` — done-claims need two independent signals.
- `agents.md`, `fan-out-contract.md` — structured subagent handoffs.
- `development-workflow.md` — plan-first entry where the start boundary fires.
